To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
EGF receptor expression is a limiting factor in the mitogenic activation of EGF‐dependent NRK cells.

1) TGF‐β and RA increase EGF‐inducible EGF receptor levels in serum‐depleted NRK cells; 2) this increase in EGF receptor levels results in a faster rate of EGF‐induction of MAP kinase activation; 3) TGF‐beta and RA increase the percentage of cells in S‐phase as a function of the duration of EGF treatment; 4) PGF‐α and BK also increased EGF receptor levels
EGF receptor density controls mitogenesis in NRK cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the growth of normal rat kidney fibroblasts (NRK cells).
the molecular mechanisms that control the growth of normal rat kidney fibroblasts (NRK cells).
the regulation of cell growth by growth factors and their receptors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the growth of the NRK cells is regulated by the density of the EGF receptors on the cell surface.
the EGF receptor is a limiting factor in EGF‐inducible mitogenic stimulation of NRK cells.
the density‐dependent growth of NRK cells is controlled by the EGF receptor, and that the EGF receptor is regulated by growth factors and hormones.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
EGF receptor levels control mitogen‐activated kinase (MAPK), which in turn controls the cell cycle.
EGF receptor levels control the mitogenic activation of EGF by NRK cells.
the growth factor receptor density controls the mitogenic response.
The main takeaway from our work is that
EGF receptor density is an important factor in controlling cell growth in normal rat kidney cells.
the EGF receptor is not only a receptor, but also a regulator of cell proliferation.
the epidermal growth receptor (EGFR) controls mitogenic activation by EGF.
